test_title: PYST 07: SSC Stenographer 2025: English Language & Comprehension (Held On: 08 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct?

options.text: When we reached the station, the train have already left.
When we reached the station, the train has already left.
When we reached the station, the train had already left.
When we reached the station, the train already left.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence describes a past event using the past tense "reached."
 
• To indicate an action that occurred before another past event, the past perfect tense ("had") is used.
 
• Option 3 correctly uses "had already left" to show that the train departed before the speakers reached the station.
 
• Other options use incorrect tenses ("have," "has," or "already left" without "had"), which do not maintain grammatical accuracy.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"When we reached the station, the train had already left."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "have" is incorrect because it is present perfect, which does not align with the past event "reached."
 
• **Option 2:** "has" is incorrect for the same reason as "have"—it does not match the past tense context.
 
• **Option 4:** "already left" without "had" fails to indicate the sequence of past events clearly.
